sentences.text: The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Sri.Munumadappa in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners case is as under:
2.

That, on 15-02-2023 at about 02-30 p.m, the deceased Munumadappa was proceeding in a new Bajaj Pulser bike, on Attibele - Anekal road, Bengaluru when he reached near Harohalli at that time, driver of Lorry bearing registration No.KA- 51/0272 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
3. It is further stated that immediately after the accident, said Munumadappa was shifted to Oxford Hospital and died in the hospital during the course of treatment.
Thereafter, post mortem was conducted and the body was handed over to the petitioners.
The petitioners have spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased.

4. It is further stated that prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 26 years and working as a driver by earning Rs.25,000/- per month and contributing the entire income towards the welfare of the family.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, petitioners have put to untold misery, pain, shock and mental agony.
5. It is further stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Lorry bearing registration No.KA-51/0272.
Hence, jurisdictional Attibele Police have filed criminal case in Cr.No.63/2023 against driver of said vehicle.
Hence, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
6. In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 & 2 were appeared through their respective counsel and filed the written statements.
7. In the written statement respondent No.1 contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing registration No.KA-51/0272 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

Further contended that, driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. F.C and permit to the said vehicle as on the date of the accident, hence there is a Badre Gowda Alias Badrappa vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54485903/
2 violation of terms and conditions of the policy.

sentences.text: Further contended that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased only, as he was not wearing the helmet and not followed the traffic rules and regulations, hence this petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.

Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and expenses incurred towards funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased and also denied the relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive and exorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.
8. The respondent No.2 in the written statement contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further he has stated that, he is the RC owner of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA- 51/0272 and got insured his vehicle with respondent No.1 the policy was in force as on the date of the accident and driver of said vehicle was having valid D.L.
Further contended that, accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased himself.

Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and expenses incurred towards funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased and also denied the relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive and exorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that, Manumadappa son of Badre Gowda @
Badrappa had died due to injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 15.2.2023 at about 2.30 p.m. near Harohalli, on Attibele, Anekal Road, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA-51- 0272 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3) What order or award?

11.

On the other hand, the driver of offending vehicle got examined as RW1 and got marked one document as Ex.R1.
12.
Heard the arguments of both the counsels.
Perused the materials available on record.

It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA- 51/0272, the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently Munumadappa had succumbed to the injuries.

15. On the other hand, the respondents have contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased and not on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA-51/0272.
16.

On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the driver of the offending vehicle in question.
17. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.2 by name Smt.Munithayamma examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit, she has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to Ex.P12.
P1 - copy of the F.I.R. Ex
.P2-copy of the first information statement given by Sri.Muniyappa,
Ex.P3-copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P4-copy of spot sketch, Ex.P5-copy of post mortem report, Ex.P6- inquest report, Ex.P7-copy of IMV report, Ex.P8-copy of charge sheet.

19. PW1 was subjected for cross-examination at length, but no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.
20. On the other hand, the respondents have examined driver of offending vehicle as RW1.

In his chief-examination RW1 has deposed that, while he was parking vehicle on foot path, at that time by consuming alcohol the deceased came on two wheeler in a rash and negligent manner and hit back side of the lorry.
The accident took place due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased only.
In his cross- examination he has admitted that accident road is a straight road and he could see the vehicles coming from back side and front side.
He was seen deceased coming on two wheeler before the accident.
It appears that, RW1 had seen the deceased prior to the accident and if he could have taken some precautions, then accident would have been avoided.
Further, he has admitted that he had not taken deceased to the hospital and ran away from the accident spot after the accident.
Ex.P4 is spot sketch wherein it discloses that deceased was coming from Attibele to Anekal and offending vehicle was coming from Anekal.
On perusal of sketch it appears that deceased was on left side of the road, but, offending lorry driver came from opposite direction and took his vehicle to left turn from extreme right side.

As a result of which, the deceased vehicle dashed the hind portion of the Badre Gowda Alias Badrappa vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54485903/
4 lorry and sustained grievous injuries.

sentences.text: It is evident from the Ex.P7 IMV report that, offending vehicle got damaged at rear right side wheel and mudguard.
Further Ex.P8 charge sheet disclose that after the investigation I.O has filed charge sheet against driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
So, it clearly establishes that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
21. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA-51/0272 and in the said accident, Munumadappa succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.
ISSUE No.2:
22.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P10 to Ex.P12 Aadhar cards of the petitioners and the deceased, which have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak that the petitioners are the parents of the deceased 23.

Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the age particulars of the petitioners, mentioned in the cause title of the petition, reflected that, the petitioners No.1 & 2 in their middle age, lost their son, as well as the care from their son, who was the backbone of the family.
The respondents herein have not produced documents on record, to show the independent economic status of the petitioners, at the time of cross-examination of the PW1.
By taking into consideration of all these factors, along with the evidence of PW1, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were the dependents to the deceased during his lifetime.
24. To prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident, the petitioners have placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P12.
On going through same, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 01.01.1997.
The said document remained unquestioned by the other side.
The alleged accident had occurred on 15.02.2023.

Hence, I am of the view that, as on the date of the accident,
the deceased was aged about 26 years.
For his age, multiplier '17' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.
25. In connection with the work of the deceased in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was working as driver and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The petitienrs have not placed any document to prove the actual income and avocation of the deceased.

Hence, it is apt to take the notional income, by looking into consideration of the year of accident along with other facts and circumstances of the case, as well as by looking in to the chart of the notional income of the Legal Services Authority.

Hence, the income of the deceased is considered as Rs.16,000/-

Another point tobe taken into consideration herein that as per the petition, the deceased was a bachelor, for deduction of the personal and living expenses, the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14 is to be considered.
27.
Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
"

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50- 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

The established income means the income minus the tax component. "
28.
Having considered the above as per law laid down in the above case.

In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, since the deceased was a bachelor,
deduction towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation is to be considered.
In the present case, deceased was aged about 26 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "17" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through main petition averments it is evident that, the deceased herein as on the date of the accident was not having permanent job.

As such by taking into consideration of the nature of the employment mentioned in the petition, I am of the view that, 40% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,000/- per month.
And Rs.1,92,000/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 40% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased, comes to (Rs.1,92,000+76,800)= Rs.2,68,800/-.
And 50% has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Thus net loss income comes to Rs.1,34,400/- (Rs.2,68,800- Rs.1,34,400/-).
This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "17".

Which comes to Rs.22,84,800/-.
29.

LIABILITY:-
34.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA-51/0272, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurance company and the respondent No.2 being the R.C. owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
35. As per the records insurance policy was valid from 09.12.2022 to 08.12.2023.
The alleged accident had taken place on 15.02.2023.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Hence, respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
36.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act, is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.24,14,112/- (Rupees twenty four lakh fourteen thousand one hundred and twelve only) along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled the share of 50% each.

Out of share amount of petitoner No.1 and 2, 40% of the amount together with interest shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank for a period of three years and the remaining 60% of of the amount shall be released to them through due process of law.

Along with this, the future prospects of 40% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased, comes to (Rs.1,92,000+76,800)= Rs.2,68,800/-.
And 50% has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
Therefore this tribunal awarded the amount of Rs.8,312/- under the head medical expenses.
